Omg a direct mention.
It should be "_global class_" across the board, probably. Most people casually say it that way, too. However, EditorFileSystem & co. seem to call it "_script class_" first, which feels like legacy baggage prone to confusion.
Maybe @Hilderin has ideas after poking quite a bit at `EditorFileSystem` logic?

Could cut `_get_name()` and just format the class name with spaces for the display name, then there's no need to instantiate scripts before a command is ran. The class name is required anyway and the command palette api is still available through plugins if display name customization is important

That feels too limiting, looking at how I would use the feature I would adopt a common naming scheme for the class names e.g. prefixing them with `Command`. I don't want that noise in the command palette.

Also just looking at one example that I actually used at one point: `CommandRecalculate3DNavigationMeshForIsometricTilemapInOpenScene` isn't a class name I want to have in my project.

Maybe we could just keep a cache of previously ran EditorScripts. If you run a script once, it gets registered in some cache file and editor will automatically add it to command palette. It's cheap, the only downside is that you need to run the script normally once.

> the only downside is that you need to run the script normally once

There is no "normal" way to run an editor script when you use an external editor. Having to switch to the built-in and run all of my 40 editor scripts before I can use them each time I make a new godot project would make this feature as good as non-existent for me. Has to be a better way 🙂

We can add option to run scripts from FileSystem dock.
Or expose some method, so external editor's extensions are able to run the scripts (idk if it's possible).
That honestly sounds very confusing UX wise. If that's the alternative I'd rather remove the `_get_name` feature.
Yeah, it would be the same as not showing any scenes in the Ctrl+Shift+A dialog before the user instantiates them through the filesystem dock
So I actually tested this with a big™ project and this doesn't cause performance problems. It only checks global classes and it's even cached, so...

body:
Including classes without class name is infeasible it would require implementing a completely new cache for this, that's not worth the complexity and bug surface for this feature. 

The PR did originally feature a `_get_name` function, but it was removed due to performance concerns (it would require loading and instantiating the script which might easily get out of hand in bigger and complex projects). Once again I'm not aware of any API that would allow to create a simple and convenient cache for this.

See https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/discussions/11549 for my idea to improve on that. If a solution to build easy caches ever gets implemented this feature could be extended in scope. But it's quite helpful as is IMO
